newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia financial futures volume rises-Negara.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia financial futures volume rises-Negara.

text.p: Trading volume on the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange (KLOFFE) totalled 77,281 contracts, or a daily average turnover of 312 contracts in 1996, Malaysia's central bank said on Friday.
The KLOFFE trades the Kuala Lumpur Composite Index futures contract which was launched in December 1995.
In its 1996 annual report, Bank Negara said KLOFFE achieved a record monthly volume of 10,665 contracts in December last year, 353 percent higher than the number of trades registered in January 1996.
Foreign institutions accounted for 53 percent of the trades on KLOFFE in 1996, as domestic investors were less exposed to derivatives trading, it said.
Malaysia's other futures market product, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) contract, also reported encouraging volume, Bank Negara said.

Launched in May last year, the market recorded a turnover of 40,933 contracts or an average daily volume of 273 contracts for 1996. "By international standards, this was somewhat promising. In some futures markets, it was usual to record an average daily volume of less than 100 contracts during the first year," said the central bank.

It said market-makers accounted for 46 percent of the total volume transacted, followed by domestic financial institutions and corporations (23 percent), individuals (21 percent) and foreigners (10 percent).
